pr_title: initialize extended stack frame on RV32M1 ri5cy core
pr_body:
The optional SOC_CONTEXT carries processor state registers that need to
be initialized properly to avoid uninitialized memory read as processor
state.
In particular on the RV32M1 the extra soc context stores a state for
special loop instructions, and loading non zero values will have the
core assume it is in a loop.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/26030

issue_context.title: RV32M1_RI5CY: tests/kernel/threads/thread_apis and thread_init fails
issue_context.body:
Executing tests/kernel/threads/thread_apis and thread_init fails on the ri5cy core. The issue is an unitialized context that gets loaded into the processors hardware loop state registers lpstart0/1, lpend0/1 and lpcount0/1 when the memory is non-zero, for example after a soft reset.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. mkdir build; cd build
2. west build -b rv32m1_vega_ri5cy ~/zephyrproject/zephyr/tests/kernel/threads/thread_apis/ -- -G"Eclipse CDT4 - Ninja" -DCMAKE_REQUIRED_FLAGS=-Wl,-dT=/dev/null
3. west flash
4. CPU keeps resetting during the test. If it does not try resetting a few times with the button, eventually it will get into the reset loop


**Impact**
This affects a range of multi threading applications and it's behavior is hard to predict. On a coldstarting system there is a chance for the application to still work if the threads were created early and on zeroed memory.
One example situation impacted by it is the spi_loopback test, see #20589. This issues seems to not be isolated to an unitialized context though

review_comments: If they are all zero, do you even need this #define?

Thanks for the review!

Not really, in the Kconfig it is documented as mandatory though
```
config RISCV_SOC_CONTEXT_SAVE
...
	  Enabling this option requires that the SoC provide a
	  soc_context.h header which defines the following macros:
...
	  - SOC_ESF_INIT: structure contents initializer for struct soc_esf
	    state. The last initialized member should not end in a comma.
```
Right now RV32M1_RI5CY is the only soc actually using this feature, so SOC_ESF_INIT could just be removed and it could be hardcoded to zero initialize. If any other core were to use the RISCV_SOC_CONTEXT_SAVE feature a static constant initializer might not fit all use cases anyways, as the init values on the stack could be runtime dependent. Should I just go ahead and replace it with a memset to 0?

I am unsure why this initially assigned `0xdeadband` here, it seems to have been the default context init value. But it wasn't really used to initialize the extended stack frame before. I tried to align it with the intention according to the documentation in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/arch/riscv/Kconfig#L51 .
This config is `default y if SOC_OPENISA_RV32M1_RI5CY`, so the extra ifdef seems redundant? Are you setting `CONFIG_SOC_OPENISA_RV32M1_RI5CY=n` explicitly?

I understood it to be an option, defaulting to y, but also allowing n. So one can explicitly disable it if desired, as in less context switch overhead but not getting the benefit of the hardware loop optimization.

I did end up disabling it in a few intermediate configurations when trying to narrow the problem down, to figure out if it was a compiler issue with the hardware loops or the loop registers getting messed up during context switching and it helped there.

Personally I am not attached to having it as an option, just felt it was broken as is thus added this somewhat ugly additional ifdef level
Guess I didn't fully answer the question. After fixing the root cause by zero initializing the loop registers in the stack frame I do not set `CONFIG_SOC_OPENISA_RV32M1_RI5CY=n` explicitly :-)

@MaureenHelm Sorry I just reread this, i totally referenced the wrong config symbol.
The issue at hand is not `CONFIG_SOC_OPENISA_RV32M1_RI5CY`, but `CONFIG_RISCV_SOC_CONTEXT_SAVE`. It is `default y`, but can be configured to false if desired, to avoid the overhead of the stack operations if one doesn't use the loop optimization feature of the RI5CY core. This commit fixes `CONFIG_RISCV_SOC_CONTEXT_SAVE=n`. I can remove the change if you feel it doesn't need to be supported.
